content.text: In this lesson, you will learn the basic vocabulary, phrases, and sentence structures commonly used in everyday conversations in Tagalog.

Learn to introduce yourself and ask basic questions:

list.item: Ano ang pangalan mo?: What is your name?
Saan ka nag-aaral?: Where do you study?
Taga saan ka?: Where are you from?

content.text: These phrases will help you when you need to ask for clarification or express basic ideas:

list.item: May tanong po ako. - I have a question.
Ano ang major mo? - What's your major? (Used in school contexts)
Ano ang trabaho mo? - What is your job?

content.text: Learn how to greet someone based on the time of day:

list.item: Umaga: Morning (Magandang umaga po! - Good morning!)
Tanghali: Noon (Magandang tanghali po! - Good midday/noon!)
Hapon: Afternoon (Magandang hapon po! - Good afternoon!)
Gabi: Evening (Magandang gabi po! - Good evening!)

content.text: Sentence structure in Tagalog generally follows a pattern of:
ENGLISH: Anna fried the chicken in the kitchen.
TAGALOG: Prinito ni Anna ang manok sa kusina.
Explanation: In Tagalog, the verb (action) comes first, followed by the actor (who performed the action), the object (what was acted upon), and the location.
